correctness.rationale: The integral Stirling-basis reduction gives a finite power-sum congruence for each modulus. The exact coefficients a(6)=1431665 and a(8)=6646603073 imply B=2 modulo 4. For odd bases, binomial expansion of j^2=1+8 beta gives the upper shift 2^(r-3) modulo 2^r and a half-shift residue 2^(r-1) at every even n>=r, proving minimality and exact valuations. The small powers are separately classified. Standalone integer checks returned VERIFY_OK 393; finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact dyadic least-period hierarchy is a natural invariant of a sequence whose modular periodicity was a named arithmetic problem. Existing literature gives only a nonsharp Carmichael bound plus one example. The proof resolves all powers of two and gives exact dyadic difference valuations forcing optimality, enabling arithmetic predictions at arbitrary precision. It does not merely relabel a known theorem or extrapolate a finite table.
